title: Commitment ledger
description: The lodged registration decomposed into atomic checkable obligations — the second spine beside the artefact spine (planning/audit-and-completion-plan.md § 6.6; planning/audit-charter.md § 7 Phase 1). Authored from the three lodged documents only (docs/methodology/preregistration/osf/, per osf/README.md:3,9-11); retrospective for this project, at-lodgement for future ones. Every statement is a verbatim span from the lodged text, mechanically verified by scripts/validate_commitments.py. A trigger commitment that cannot state all five trigger-rule elements fails validation at authoring time (the H7 lesson: a trigger that cannot say how 'better' is characterised must not create an obligation).

source_documents.description: The lodged documents this ledger decomposes, pinned by git blob so drift is detectable.

git_blob.description: Abbreviated git blob hash of the lodged file at decomposition time.

commitment_id.description: Stable primary key, sequential in source order at first authoring; never renumbered once the ledger is committed.

source.description: Locator into the lodged text. Lines are 1-indexed and inclusive; the verbatim statement must appear within them.

section.description: Nearest enclosing heading, e.g. 'H7' or '3.1 Significance Testing'.

kind.description: Plan § 6.6 vocabulary. hypothesis = a registered prediction; condition = an experimental cell that must be run; factor = a factor/level definition constraining what may be run; trigger = a decision rule creating a conditional obligation; analysis = a statistical procedure or reporting obligation; disclosure = an explicit exclusion, caveat, or deviation licence in the lodged text.

statement.description: VERBATIM span from the lodged text — never paraphrase. Mechanically verified against the cited lines.

normalised_obligation.description: One-sentence plain restatement of what must be done or reported. Explicitly NOT verbatim; convenience only, carries no authority.

hypothesis.description: Hypothesis tag where applicable (H1–H15, H4b, HN-only); null for cross-cutting commitments.

decision_statistic.description: The statistic that discharges or tests this commitment (plan § 6.6), e.g. 'F1@20m', 'MCC', 'permutation p, FDR-corrected'. Null only for kinds with nothing to compute (e.g. disclosure).

uncertainty_treatment.description: How uncertainty is handled when assessing the commitment (plan § 6.6, the H7 lesson), e.g. 'bootstrap 95% CI, 10k iterations, seed 42', 'BH-FDR q<0.05'.

trigger.description: Required (non-null) when kind=trigger; must be null otherwise.

status.description: open = promised, not yet discharged and not waived (drift_check warns on these at every regeneration); discharged = executed/reported, evidence in discharged_by; waived = formally amended away by an erratum named in waiver.

evidence.description: Free-text pointer where manifest ids alone are insufficient (e.g. a results artefact path).

waiver.description: Erratum number licensing non-execution or amendment. Validated to exist in protocol-errata.md.

notes.description: Cross-references (e.g. the § 7 summary-table line duplicating this commitment), ambiguities, or extraction caveats.

triggerRule.description: The five-element trigger rule (audit-charter § 7 Phase 1). All five must be present and non-empty for a trigger to create an obligation — a trigger that cannot state them fails at authoring time.
